name: Yosemite Wilderness Backpacking
tagline: For backpackers taking a multi-night wilderness trip in Yosemite National Park on a trailhead-quota permit.
description: Covers a 2-5 night summer backpacking trip from a Yosemite trailhead such as Happy Isles, Lyell Canyon or Cathedral Lakes for a small group. Assumes July-September conditions with snow mostly gone, afternoon thunderstorms possible and bear canister rules in force. Adapt insulation and traction for early-season snow, and add Half Dome gear only if your permit includes the cables.
considerations: Wilderness permits are quota-limited: 60% are reserved by lottery 24 weeks ahead and 40% release 7 days ahead on Recreation.gov; walk-up permits are scarce late April to mid-October (NPS, as of 2026).
Approved bear-resistant canisters are mandatory throughout the Yosemite wilderness and hanging food is illegal; only models on the park's allowed list count (NPS list current as of July 2026).
Camp at least 100 ft from water and trails, 4 trail miles from Yosemite Valley, Tuolumne Meadows or Glacier Point, and 1 mile from any road; group limit 15 on trail, 8 off-trail.
Campfires are allowed only in existing rings below 9,600 ft and are banned in listed basins and on Half Dome; check current fire restrictions before you go.
Pack out all toilet paper; bury human waste 4-6 in deep at least 100 ft from water, trails and camp.
Half Dome cables require a separate permit even for backpackers (request it with your wilderness permit); nearly all fatal cable falls happened on wet rock.
Snow typically covers high trails November through May; expect afternoon thunderstorms and mosquitoes in early summer. Check current trail conditions and the 14-night May 1-Sept 15 stay limit.

sources.title: Half Dome Day Hike and Permits

items.text: Yosemite wilderness permit for your trailhead and entry date
items.note: Lottery opens 24 weeks ahead; 40% of each quota releases 7 days ahead on Recreation.gov (as of 2026).

items.text: Half Dome permit if your route includes the cables
items.note: Needed even for backpackers when the cables are up; request it with the wilderness permit.

items.text: Photo ID and permit confirmation for pickup at a wilderness center
Park entry reservation if one is in effect for your dates
items.note: Yosemite has used peak-period entry reservations in recent years; check the current rules.

items.text: Itinerary with a legal first-night camp (4 trail miles from developed areas)
items.note: Share it with an emergency contact along with your exit date.

items.text: Check current trail, snow and river-crossing conditions
Check current fire restrictions and air quality (wildfire smoke)
Topographic map and route plan with bailout trailheads
Lodging or campsite plan for the night before your start
Approved bear-resistant canister (about one per 1-2 people)
items.note: Hanging food is illegal park-wide. Garcia 812 rentals only at the Valley Welcome Center; Ursack is not on the allowed list.

items.text: All food, trash and scented toiletries fit inside the canister
items.note: Includes sunscreen, bug spray, lip balm, medications and feminine products.

items.text: Store the canister 25-50 ft from camp on level ground, away from cliffs and water
Food repackaged into bags to save canister space
Bear-aware routine: cook away from the tent and never leave food unattended
items.note: Food must be stored unless within arm's reach of an awake person.

items.text: Tent with rainfly and footprint
Sleeping bag rated to about 20-30 F
Insulated sleeping pad
Extra guylines and stakes for granite slabs and wind
Pillow and earplugs
Broken-in boots or trail shoes
Wool or synthetic socks (3 pairs)
Rain jacket
items.note: Afternoon thunderstorms are common in summer.

items.text: Insulating layer (fleece or puffy)
Base layers, hiking pants or shorts, sun shirt
Warm hat and gloves
Sun hat and sunglasses
Camp shoes or sandals for stream crossings
Grippy gloves for the Half Dome cables (pack them out)
items.note: Discarded gloves pile up at the base of the cables; carry yours out.

items.text: Water filter or purification treatment
Bottles or bladder for 2-3 liters
Stove and enough fuel for the trip
items.note: Wood-burning stoves are not allowed where campfires are prohibited.

items.text: Pot, spoon and mug
Meals for every day plus one extra day
Snacks and electrolyte mix
Small bottle of biodegradable soap, used 100 ft from water
Map and compass, or GPS app with offline maps
Headlamp with spare batteries
First aid kit with blister care
Satellite messenger or PLB
items.note: No reliable cell service in the wilderness.

items.text: Sunscreen SPF 30+ and lip balm (stored in the canister at night)
Insect repellent and head net (early summer)
Whistle, knife and repair tape
Trekking poles
Microspikes or ice axe for early-season passes
Thunderstorm plan: summit early and avoid exposed rock when storms build
Trowel for a 4-6 in cathole 100 ft from water, trails and camp
Bags to pack out all toilet paper and hygiene products
items.note: Toilet paper may not be buried or burned in Yosemite.

items.text: Trash bag; pack out everything you bring in
Camp on durable surfaces at least 100 ft from water and trails
Fires only in existing rings below 9,600 ft; drown ashes cold
items.note: Prefer a stove; check current fire restrictions.

items.text: Leave drones and pets at home (prohibited in the wilderness)
